name: opencode
readmeHtml:
The open source AI coding agent.

English | 简体中文 | 繁體中文 | 한국어 | Deutsch | Español | Français | Italiano | Dansk | 日本語 | Polski | Русский | Bosanski | العربية | Norsk | Português (Brasil) | ไทย | Türkçe | Українська | বাংলা | Ελληνικά | Tiếng Việt

Installation

# YOLO
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash

# Package managers
npm i -g @opencode/cli@latest      # or bun/pnpm/yarn
brew install anomalyco/tap/opencode-v2 # macOS and Linux (recommended, always up to date)
brew install opencode              # macOS and Linux (official brew formula, updated less)
sudo pacman -S opencode            # Arch Linux (Stable)
paru -S opencode-beta              # Arch Linux (Latest from AUR)
mise use -g opencode               # Any OS
nix run github:anomalyco/opencode  # Nix

Tip

Remove versions older than 0.1.x before installing.

Desktop App (BETA)

OpenCode is also available as a desktop application. Download it from opencode.ai/download.

Platform Download
macOS (Apple Silicon) opencode-desktop-mac-arm64.dmg
macOS (Intel) opencode-desktop-mac-x64.dmg
Windows opencode-desktop-win-x64.exe
Linux .deb, .rpm, or .AppImage 
# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install --cask opencode-desktop

Installation Directory

The install script installs OpenCode to $HOME/.opencode/bin.

Agents

OpenCode includes two built-in agents you can switch between with the Tab key.

  • build - Default, full-access agent for development work
  • plan - Read-only agent for analysis and code exploration
    • Denies file edits by default
    • Asks permission before running bash commands
    • Ideal for exploring unfamiliar codebases or planning changes

Also included is a general subagent for complex searches and multistep tasks. This is used internally and can be invoked using @general in messages.

Learn more about agents.

Documentation

For more info on how to configure OpenCode, head over to our docs.

Contributing

If you're interested in contributing to OpenCode, please read our contributing docs before submitting a pull request.

Building on OpenCode

If you are working on a project that's related to OpenCode and is using "opencode" as part of its name, for example "opencode-dashboard" or "opencode-mobile", please add a note to your README to clarify that it is not built by the OpenCode team and is not affiliated with us in any way.

Join our community Discord | X.com

releases.name: v2.2.0
releases.body:
### Highlights

- Create, install and share [Desktop plugins](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/gui) (experimental) ([#55246](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/55246), [#59469](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59469), [#59489](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59489))
- Refreshed the desktop app experience ([#56898](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/56898), [#58865](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58865), [#55838](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/55838), [#57962](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57962))
- Add experimental image and decision generation APIs to plugins and sdk, allowing image generation or decision model (think typesafe, clef, etc) workflows. ([#59190](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59190), [#59380](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59380), [#58758](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/58758))
- Plugins can now attach and update keyed session instructions with ctx.session.instructions.entry.put/list/remove. Instead of editing the system prompt and busting the prompt cache, each change is added as a small update at the next step. The entries also survive compaction a

releases.name: v1.19.4
releases.body:
## Core

### Improvements
- Upgraded the bundled Bun runtime to 1.4.4, which includes [security fixes](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4.4#security) for Brotli, TLS, HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, HTTP/3, WebSocket, and `fetch`, and updates root certificates to NSS 3.131.1.

releases.name: v1.19.3
releases.body:
## Core

### Improvements
- Configure model reasoning options to generate reasoning variants, replacing catalog variants while preserving your configured variant overrides.

releases.name: v1.19.2
releases.body:
## Core

### Bugfixes
- OpenCode 1 now stays on the 1.x release line: update checks use only the npm `opencode-ai` latest version, so 1.x installs are never offered a 2.x build as a regular update.
- Upgrading to OpenCode 2 remains a separate, explicit choice through the 2.0 offer in `/update` or `opencode upgrade --major`.
- Fix upgrades for installs managed by yarn.
- Skip 1.x updates for Homebrew Core installs, which now track OpenCode 2, and check tap and Chocolatey availability before offering an update.
- The install script refuses to install 2.x versions.

releases.name: v1.19.1
releases.body:
## Core

### Bugfixes
- Session sharing has been discontinued. Existing share links and session-sharing commands are no longer available, and importing sessions from share URLs is unsupported.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source AI coding agent providing an accessible alternative to proprietary coding assistants.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: OpenCode is a robust, open-source AI coding agent meticulously designed to assist developers with writing, analyzing, and managing complex codebases. It serves as a highly transparent, community-driven alternative to tightly closed-ecosystem proprietary coding assistants. The agent integrates deeply into standard developer workflows to automate boilerplate generation, suggest improvements, and analyze existing structures. By supporting multiple languages for both its documentation and primary interface, it heavily promotes global accessibility. It is actively developed, distributed via npm, and designed to drastically enhance overall programming productivity.
keyFeatures: Open-source architecture: Provides complete transparency and control over the underlying behavior.
Deep workflow integration: Embeds seamlessly into existing developer environments to provide contextual code suggestions.
Multilingual support: Offers comprehensive documentation and interface localizations to assist non-English speaking teams.
Automated boilerplate generation: Rapidly generates repetitive code structures to drastically accelerate development.
Community-driven development: Relies on active open-source contributions to continuously improve tools.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software developers, engineering teams, and open-source advocates seeking a customizable AI coding assistant. It is ideal for users who prioritize transparency and avoid reliance on closed proprietary ecosystems.
